rows.verified: Possession of a specified animal pathogen requires the relevant licence under the SAPO licensing regime.
Licence conditions are intended to prevent release or escape of specified animal pathogens into the environment.
Licence holders must complete a risk assessment for activities involving specified animal pathogens.
Containment and control measures must be proportionate and effective for the pathogen and work.
Management arrangements must support effective application and maintenance of containment controls.
Facilities should define responsibilities, competence and supervision for licensed pathogen work.
Emergency procedures should address spills, loss of containment, exposure and potential environmental release.
Records, monitoring and review should demonstrate continued compliance with licence conditions.
Specified-pathogen risk depends on agent, strain, quantity, procedure, containment level, equipment, personnel and emergency capability.
SAPO evidence is agent-, facility-, process-, containment- and incident-specific and is not an exact parcel-level release probability.
Commercial supply, hire and use of play inflatables are subject to health-and-safety law.
Outdoor inflatables should not be operated above the manufacturer's maximum wind speed and never above 24 mph where that general limit applies.
Outdoor wind speed must be measured with an anemometer at regular intervals; smartphone weather applications are not a substitute.
All required anchor points must be used with suitable stakes, ballast or rated anchors.
Inflation pressure and blower condition must remain within the manufacturer's operating limits.
The inflatable should be checked before use for damage, deformation, secure connections and safe deflation behaviour.
At least one suitably trained person should constantly supervise normal play-inflatable use.
Initial testing and annual inspection by a competent person are required to confirm continuing safe condition.
Play-inflatable risk depends on device design, wind, anchoring, pressure, surface, user mix, supervision, maintenance and emergency response.
Inflatable evidence is device-, site-, weather-, operator-, user- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
